The horizontal semicircular canal ocular reflex is indeed influenced by otolith organs input. The question posed explicitly asks about this topic, covering each sub-question within the response:

The plane of compensatory eye movements induced by the horizontal semicircular canal stimulation does not always parallel to the canal axis due to the influence of otolith organs on the reflex. This means that the orientation of eye movements can vary depending on how well the brain has processed the input from the otolith organs, which are responsible for detecting changes in head position and movement.

In summary, the horizontal semicircular canal ocular reflex is affected by the input from otolith organs, leading to variations in compensatory eye movements.
